title: How Long Would You Last Inside the Sun's Corona? #shorts
description_hook: You're floating 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface, inside a corona of 2 million °C, with no suit. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last inside the Sun's corona? You're 6.1 million km from the surface. The gas around you is 2 million °C.
beats.img: a tiny human silhouette floating in black space before a gigantic glowing solar surface, wispy white coronal streamers curling outward all around

beats.say: But it's 10 million times thinner than the surface. Too thin to burn you. The light is the problem.
beats.img: faint pearly strands of thin plasma drifting through dark space near the Sun, a few scattered glowing particles, soft eerie glow

beats.say: Sunlight here is about 475 times brighter than on Earth. Your skin takes the full blast.
beats.img: a blinding wall of white sunlight flooding the frame, a dark outstretched hand silhouetted against the overwhelming glare

beats.say: And there's no air. After about 9 to 11 seconds, you black out. The water on your tongue starts to boil.
beats.img: a lone figure in plain clothes drifting limp in empty space, back to the camera, a huge orange solar disk filling the background

beats.say: Within 1 minute, your blood stops circulating. The Sun doesn't even notice.
beats.img: a vast churning solar surface with a towering looping prominence, seen from close orbit, no trace of anything human in sight

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. Parker zips past at 692,000 km/h, behind a shield rated to 1,377 °C.
